title: INTERSECT
description: INTERSECT returns only the rows that appear in BOTH result sets. Write a query that returns the `customer_id` of every customer who has BOTH placed at least one order AND had at least one appointment.
hints: SELECT customer_id FROM orders is one set of ids, SELECT customer_id FROM appointments is another - INTERSECT keeps only the ids present in both, the same idea as Python's set.intersection().
Select customer_id from orders, put INTERSECT between the two queries, then select customer_id from appointments.
expected_behavior: Returns the distinct customer_id values present in both orders and appointments.
solution: SELECT customer_id FROM orders INTERSECT SELECT customer_id FROM appointments;
explanation: INTERSECT is less commonly needed than UNION but is exactly the right tool for "which rows exist in both of these result sets" questions - the alternative (an INNER JOIN or a WHERE ... IN subquery) works too, but INTERSECT states the intent most directly.
